# PLAN — iteration 2

## Current state assessment

Iteration 1 passed the unchanged behavioral and tool gates and met timing, but retained 16 LUTs, matching the timing-feasible incumbent, so it failed the strict LUT-reduction objective. Its proposed inline, factored parallel XOR update did not reduce LUT usage. The current seed is still a wrapper around the frozen core; the routed baseline uses 16 LUTs and 34 FFs, with WNS 0.445 ns and WHS 0.208 ns.

## Hypothesis

A shared, bit-serial CRC update using the existing CRC state and data inputs may map the polynomial feedback and shift into fewer LUTs than the already-tried factored parallel XOR network, at the cost of a deeper combinational path that must still close at 10 ns.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the wrapper instance with equivalent top-level slot and CRC state logic, preserving the one-slot ready equation, synchronous active-high reset priority, registered outputs, and `// @latency 1`. Implement the byte update as an explicitly shared eight-step MSB-first feedback recurrence, reusing each step’s feedback term across the polynomial taps; do not repeat the iteration 1 factored parallel XOR equations. Preserve frame restart on `in_last`, stalled output stability, and reset behavior, and rely on routed LUT, setup, and hold reports to determine whether this distinct mapping improves the objective.
